grading_system.evidence: A student meets the requirements for graduation by providing evidence of proficiency credit in all required curriculum areas. Each Vergennes Union High School graduate will meet graduation requirements through a minimum of 22.5 credits

schedule.evidence: Each year of high school, students typically earn up to 8 credits through their daily course schedule. Courses are semester-based (Add/drop during first five days of each semester); the catalog does not state how many courses run at once, so courses_per_term is null.

credit_definition.text: Course units are labeled 'Block/credit': 1 Block/credit for a full-year course, .5 Block/credit for a semester course (so one semester course = .5 credit).
credit_definition.evidence: Driver Education .5 Block/credit Grades 9-12 (course listing; semester courses carry .5 credit)

course_load.evidence: Students typically earn up to 8 credits through their daily course schedule.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Credits are the catalog's unit and standard credits (1 = full-year course); no conversion needed. Area minimums: English 4, Math 3, Science 3, Social Studies 3 (incl. US History 1 and Civics .5), Visual/Performing Arts 1, PE 1.5, Health .5, Technology .5, Financial Literacy .5, Electives 5.5.

flexible_pathways_listed: online courses (VTVLC and other approved online programs)
Mount Abraham Union High School courses
notes: Flexible pathways require prior approval and must appear in the student's Personalized Learning Plan. Proficiency is scored on a final course score (2.5 or higher earns proficiency credit); the numeric scale is in a separate Proficiency-Based Learning guide, not in this catalog. Transferable skills are assessed within academic classes. Required content areas for proficiency: literacy, mathematics, scientific inquiry, global citizenship, physical education, artistic expression, transferable skills. Individualized alternate pathways (IEP, Multi Year Plan) are referred to the Student and Family Handbook. Catalog is the 2026-27 Program of Studies (updated 8/26).
